Maths at work

Construction and the built environment

Jobs in this route, and the maths they use.

Ratio

Bricklayer

Construction and the built environment

\(0.3 \div 6 = 0.05\) m³ per part

Concrete for a shed base is often mixed \(1 : 2 : 3\): 1 part cement, 2 parts sand, 3 parts gravel, in buckets of the same size. You need 0.3 m³ of dry mix.

  1. Total parts: \(1 + 2 + 3 = 6\).
  2. One part: \(0.3 \div 6 = 0.05\) m³.
  3. Cement 0.05 m³, sand 0.10 m³, gravel 0.15 m³.

Percentages

Plumber

Construction and the built environment

\(\pounds 350 \times 1.2 = \pounds 420\)

A VAT-registered plumber adds 20% VAT to the bill. To add 20%, multiply by 1.2. The job costs £350 before VAT.

  1. \(\pounds 350 \times 1.2 = \pounds 420\).
  2. The VAT is £70.

Electrician

Construction and the built environment

\(5.4 \div 230 \times 100 = 2.3\%\)

Voltage drops along a long cable. The wiring rules (BS 7671) allow at most 3% on a lighting circuit and 5% on others. The UK supply is 230 V.

  1. Most allowed on lighting: \(3\% \text{ of } 230 = 0.03 \times 230 = 6.9\) V.
  2. A lighting circuit drops 5.4 V. As a percentage: \(5.4 \div 230 \times 100 = 2.3\%\).
  3. 2.3% is under 3%, so it passes.

Area and perimeter

Painter and decorator

Construction and the built environment

\(64 \div 16 = 4\) litres

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

A room is 4 m by 3.5 m, with walls 2.5 m high. There is a 2 m² door and a 3.5 m² window. Two coats; the tin says 1 litre covers 16 m² (example figure).

  1. Perimeter: \(4 + 3.5 + 4 + 3.5 = 15\) m.
  2. Wall area: \(15 \times 2.5 = 37.5\) m².
  3. Take away door and window: \(37.5 - 5.5 = 32\) m².
  4. Two coats: 64 m². Paint: \(64 \div 16 = 4\) litres.
